contract: tier-c-approval/v1 admission and dispatch, with the runtime-config/v2 approval timeout bound
note: `proposal` is the proposal every sequence replays unless the sequence overrides a field: `created_at_ms` and `expires_at_ms` are the wall-clock audit record, and `created_mono_ms` is the creating process's monotonic clock at creation, so its monotonic deadline is `created_mono_ms` plus the proposal's lifetime. `reply` is an operator reply on `path` (`remote`, `console` or `offline_token`, the last carrying its `token` claims) at monotonic `mono_ms` and wall-clock `wall_ms`, with `commit` `ok` or `held` for whether its durable commit succeeded and `reservation` `unavailable` when the commit could not reserve the terminal uncertainty record, and with `proposal` naming a later proposal a `propose` step opened when the reply is to that one; `dispatch` is the live attempt beginning dispatch, with `marker_durable` whether its `dispatch_started` record reached the store and `unavailable` the writers and services that are not available, none of which it waits for, and `pending_at_ceiling` when the pending-outcome ceiling has been reached; `outcome` is the outcome write, with `write` `ok`, `blocked` while the writer is held, or `failed` when the outcome cannot be appended, and `result` `executed`, `failed` when the executor affirms the commanded physical outcome did not occur, or `timeout`, `lost_response`, `partial` or `indeterminate`, none of which establishes the physical outcome; `crash` ends the process, with `non_dispatch_record` when an affirmative durable record that dispatch was never invoked had been committed; `restart` starts a new process, whose monotonic clock is unrelated to the old one; `binding_change` changes the in-force commissioned binding or authority snapshot; `reconcile` presents a reconciliation from `source`, an `operator_local` one carrying the request of `evidence reconcile-tier-c` in cli-commands/v1, with `installed_operator_uid` the installed operator identity (whose vectors, and whose `caller` shape, are cli-commands/vectors/tier-c-reconcile.json); `propose` asks whether a later proposal of `tier`, `outcome` and `zone` is admitted, and with `opens` creates it under that name when it is. `create` with `commit` `failed` is a proposal row that could not be committed, after which no proposal exists; `alert_result` is the alert provider's answer to the latest attempt, `delivered` or `ambiguous`. `reserved` is whether the terminal uncertainty record reserved at admission is held, `later` the state of each later proposal by name, and `later_safe_default_intents` how many safe-default intents each one created. `actuations` counts physical actuations, `safe_default` whether a safe-default intent exists and `safe_default_intents` how many were created, `alert_attempts` the proposal identifier each alert attempt carried, `log_records` the durable log records of the safe default, `proposal_sent` whether a proposal reached the operator, `safe_default_attempted` and `safe_default_recorded` whether the safe default was attempted and whether it was claimed durable, `events` the CRITICAL events raised, `notice` the last operator notice, `records` the durable decision records in append order, `action_records` the runtime-health/v2 counts, `unknown_live` among them, `evidence_status` what they make evidence health, and `token_consumed` whether the step's `token_id` is claimed. `config_cases` are `approval_timeout_seconds` values against a release maximum. `safe_default_cases` name a Tier C `safe_default_action`, the `tier` it resolves to, its `capability` as the runtime guard classifies it (`informational`, `host_state`, `physical` when any executor, command or transport it invokes can change physical state, or `unclassified` for an action the guard has not classified), and only an action classified `informational` can be admitted, and its action-registry entry as `registry` (`null` for an action the registry does not govern), and whether a proposal carrying it can exist; `registry` carries the entry's `minimum_tier`, `physical`, `consequence_class` and `safe_default_eligible`, and an action with none is refused. The `registry` values of the named runtime actions pin the ori-runtime registry; `unflagged_valve_command`, `ungoverned_actuator_command` and `flagged_notifier` are hypothetical actions whose registry entry disagrees with their capability, or that have none; `unclassed_notifier` is a hypothetical informational action whose registry entry carries no consequence class; `alert_sms_raised` is a hypothetical informational action a skill declared above Tier A, `tier_a_host_probe` a hypothetical Tier A action that changes host state, and `unclassified_hook_action` a hypothetical action with no registry entry that the guard has not classified, which the ori-runtime registry today treats as safe-default eligible. The actions safety-profile/vectors/legacy-actions.json names, the outcomes they map to, and `coap_command` are the pinned instance tier-c-approval/v1 names. The offline-token sequences are offline-tokens/vectors/tier-c-binding.json. `proposal_scope_cases` name a proposed action, its `tier`, whether it can change physical state (`capability`), the commissioned `zone` and `commissioned_outcome` it names, and whether tier-c-approval/v1 governs it, refuses it, or leaves it outside the contract on the existing workflow. `authority_snapshot_cases` are authority snapshots, as an object or as raw `snapshot_text`, each valid with the SHA-256 of its canonical bytes or malformed.

sequences.name: a live approval dispatches immediately and records its outcome
a held state-store writer leaves the reply unapproved and nothing executes
a blocked outcome writer never delays or repeats the action; the approval survives and the outcome is unknown
a reply after the monotonic deadline is not an approval
expiry between commit and dispatch ends execution authority with the non-actuating safe default
a crash before the executor call with an affirmative non-dispatch record is aborted and kept
a durable approval with neither marker nor proof is dispatch_not_proven after restart, and never replayed
a relay that actuated while its marker lost the race is dispatch_not_proven, never aborted
a durable marker without an outcome is dispatch_outcome_unknown, and a restart after dispatch began never replays
a duplicate reply is idempotent
the local console and an offline token use the same admission boundary
stopped or disabled evidence never delays dispatch after the approval commit
an unauthenticated reply changes nothing
a refused proposal applies only the non-actuating safe default
a contention refusal at dispatch never actuates and applies only the safe default
a failed actuation is recorded dispatch_failed, never executed
a forward wall-clock jump does not shorten execution authority
a backward wall-clock jump does not extend execution authority
a backward wall-clock jump between commit and dispatch does not extend execution authority
a restart with an open proposal closes it proposal_aborted_restart, and no later reply revives it from expires_at_ms
an uncertain dispatch blocks only the same outcome on the same zone
dispatch_not_proven blocks the same way and Tier D always continues
an authenticated local operator command reconciles by appending, and the same outcome is admitted again
unauthenticated operator input and uncommissioned feedback reconcile nothing
commissioned feedback for the zone reconciles dispatch_not_proven
a changed commissioned binding makes the reply no approval and applies no physical action
a changed authority snapshot makes the reply no approval
a binding changed back after a mismatch revives nothing
an unchanged binding and authority admit the approval
a restart repeated after proposal_aborted_restart creates one safe-default intent
replies after approval_binding_changed create one safe-default intent and never the proposed action
a timeout result is dispatch_outcome_unknown, never dispatch_failed, and is never replayed
a lost response result is dispatch_outcome_unknown, never dispatch_failed, and is never replayed
a partial result is dispatch_outcome_unknown, never dispatch_failed, and is never replayed
an indeterminate result is dispatch_outcome_unknown, never dispatch_failed, and is never replayed
the approval commit reserves a terminal uncertainty record, released by a recorded outcome
a reply whose uncertainty record cannot be reserved is not an approval
a full pending structure leaves a live unknown that is not durable, with no dispatch delay and no replay
an outcome that cannot be appended stays pending while live, is never claimed durable, and resolves at restart by the marker
a later proposal for a blocked outcome is refused at creation and none is opened
an uncertainty arising after a later proposal was created blocks its reply, and only its outcome and zone
reconciliation after a blocked reply revives nothing and admits a fresh proposal
a full pending structure without a durable marker is dispatch_not_proven after restart, never a durable unknown
a store that accepts the write while live records the outcome the executor reported
an approval in flight for the same outcome and zone blocks a later proposal's reply inside the commit
one safe-default intent per proposal: an ambiguous alert is retried with the proposal id, and a restart creates no second intent
local logging of the safe default is idempotent by proposal id across a restart
a proposal row that cannot be committed is never sent, approves nothing and claims nothing durable

config_cases.name: one second above the release maximum
a remote site extending the lifetime to a day

authority_snapshot_cases.name: a zone with no safety profile in force
a snapshot missing the policy digest
a snapshot whose version is a string
a snapshot whose zone digest is not lowercase sha256 hex
a snapshot naming a member twice

proposal_scope_cases.name: a relay trip on its commissioned zone
a CoAP-backed actuator through its commissioned zone and outcome
a generic coap_command with no zone
a generic coap_command naming a zone
a generic coap_command naming a zone and an outcome
a physical action with no commissioned zone
a host-state Tier C action stays on the existing workflow
a host-state Tier B action requiring approval
a physical Tier B action requiring approval
